brief: Hedge funds have purged technology exposure to record lows: Goldman's prime book shows the US tech long/short ratio at 1.5, down from 2.14 in June and the lowest since the series began in 2016, while BofA's survey shows net overweight Tech falling roughly -27 points, one of the steepest monthly declines on record, alongside 52% of respondents now expecting AI hyperscaler capex cuts. JPMorgan data shows hedge fund net exposure to the momentum factor has flipped slightly negative, with only quant funds still net long, and Vanda/Sober Look data puts institutional AI-equity exposure at its lowest since April 2025. With positioning this washed out, Bloomberg and LSEG data show a possible double bottom and the Nasdaq 100 back near its long-term trendline, and SentimenTrader notes that historically, once over half of Nasdaq 100 names are in a bear market, the index has gained an average 5% over the next three months 59% of the time. Meanwhile the AI spending case still holds: Goldman sees 40% to 175% upside to Nvidia and points to its roughly $227bn buyback authorization, Goldman expects AI infrastructure earnings growth to slow from near 90% to below 20% by 2029, and Morgan Stanley sees hyperscaler capex still rising, to over $1.6tn in 2027 and almost $1.8tn in 2028. The note's conclusion: positioning is washed out enough for a bounce, not that the AI spending theme itself is broken.
